Definition: to shrivel up, i.e. contract or bend the body (or neck) in deference
BiblicalUsage: Bowing the head is the body's answer to God's goodness: Abraham's servant bowed his head and worshipped when he found Rebekah, the people bowed their heads and worshipped when they heard God had looked on their affliction, Moses made haste and bowed his head toward the earth. Jehoshaphat bowed his face to the ground before the LORD.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bowed head is the right shape for worship, because it is what the body does when it knows it stands before someone greater. The bow is not fear, it is the body's Amen to a goodness too great to stand straight before.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
